what: United Rentals rents construction and industrial equipment: lifts, earthmovers, generators, trench shoring and temporary power. It is the largest equipment rental company in the world, with around 1,500 locations.
customers: Construction contractors, industrial plants, utilities, infrastructure projects and government agencies.
money: trench safety, power, fluid solutions and mobile storage
selling fleet at the end of its rental life
moat: A fleet worth tens of billions and a branch network that can deliver to any large job site, which regional competitors cannot match on national projects.
risks: Construction spending is cyclical and falls sharply in a downturn
Debt of about $16 billion funds the fleet
Equipment values fall when used-equipment markets soften
Interest rates affect both customers' projects and its own financing
opportunities: Large infrastructure, data centre and factory projects favour the only national renter
Specialty rentals grow faster and earn better margins than general equipment
Contractors increasingly rent rather than own, which shifts the market its way
watch: Fleet productivity and used-equipment sale prices, which signal where the cycle is.
